newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW - BT sees high rating for Concert.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW - BT sees high rating for Concert.

text.p: British Telecommunications Plc said on Sunday it had not met with credit rating agencies to discuss its merger with MCI Communications Corp but it expects the new entity, to be called Concert, to have a high rating.

BT group finance director Robert Brace also said cash requirements for the deal -- which amount to some 4.5 billion stg in payouts to BT and MCI shareholders -- will not be a problem as BT has several funding channels open to the company.

"BT is a strong company. MCI is a strong company. Concert will be a particularly strong company with strong cash flows. I'm sure it will have a high credit rating," Brace told Reuters in a telephone interview.
BT has triple-A ratings from both Moody's Investors Service and Standard & Poor's, while MCI is rated A by S&P.
"At this moment I've had no discussions with the rating agencies," Brace said. "Obviously we will talk to them later."
Asked if he thought it was possible the merged entity could retain the triple-A rating, Brace said, "That's for the rating agencies to decide."
A high credit rating translates into cheaper funding costs for a company, as the market typically demands less of a yield premium over government debt.

Moody's in late September affirmed its Aaa rating of BT and its guaranteed subsidiaries after BT announced an agreement with Compagnie General des Eaux for a 25 percent stake in a new French telecommunications group.
Moody's saw no effect on BT's gross debt position but it said BT's ratings were under pressure.

"BT's ratings remain under pressure due to increasing competitive factors in the UK, which could impair the group's ability to maintain stable cash flow in the intermediate term," Moody's said at the time.
Officials for Moody's and S&P could not be reached for comment on Sunday.

The merger, which is set to create a telecom giant with annual revenue of more than 25 billion stg, includes a 35p per share payout to BT shareholders and a $6.00 per share payment to MCI shareholders, who will also receive 0.54 new Concert American depositary shares) for each MCI share.
Details of the merger were formally announced on Sunday although on Friday bonds of MCI rallied on speculation a merger with BT would lead to an upgrade of MCI debt.

S&P director Frank Plumley in New York said on Friday, "In the event of a merger, we would expect the gap (between BT and MCI ratings) to close. As to where it will shake out, that will depend on the terms of the deal and the source of funding."

Brace said on Sunday that BT had a cash mountain of "three and a bit" billion pounds. He said raising the remaining amount for the payouts to BT and MCI shareholders would not be a problem as there were a number of lines open to the company.
"We have borrowing lines in place... We could borrow in the commercial paper market in the UK or the U.S.," he said. "From a financing point of view, it's not an issue."
BT also said on Sunday it had no plans to launch a rights issue to find its merger.
